slides.title: Git (Local Machine) vs. GitHub (Cloud Platform)
slides.html:
PART 01 • ARCHITECTURE

Git (Local Machine) vs. GitHub (Cloud Platform)

Distinguishing between your offline CLI engine and the world's largest developer platform

Local vs. Cloud
01

Git (The Engine)

  • ✓ Installed on your local operating system
  • ✓ 100% offline, requires zero internet access
  • ✓ Manages commit history inside .git/
  • • Cannot share code with others on its own
02

GitHub (The Cloud)

  • ✓ Cloud hosting platform for Git repositories
  • ✓ Team Pull Requests & Code Review
  • ✓ Automated CI/CD via GitHub Actions
  • ✓ Issue tracking, Kanban boards & security scans
Core Mental Model: Git is like your personal camera taking snapshots of code. GitHub is the cloud photo album where your entire team shares, reviews, and collaborates on those photos.
Local Repositories Synced to Central GitHub Hub Team Model

slides.title: The 4 Git Areas: Adding the Cloud Remote
slides.html:
PART 01 • ARCHITECTURE

The 4 Git Areas: Adding the Cloud Remote

How code moves across the 3 local stages and reaches your GitHub remote

4 Areas Model

# Pipeline from Editor to Cloud

1. Working Directory Uncommitted raw files on your computer disk
git add
2. Staging Area (Index) Curation zone of changes ready for the snapshot
git commit
3. Local Repository (.git) Permanent commit graph stored locally on machine
git push
4. Remote (GitHub) Central cloud server where teammates sync & review
Cloud Hosted
git push transfers commits from Area 3 to Area 4. git pull fetches commits from Area 4 directly down to your working tree.
Visual Transition Map: Working Tree to Remote Architecture

slides.title: GitHub Authentication: SSH Keys vs. HTTPS & PAT
slides.html:
PART 02 • SETUP & AUTH

GitHub Authentication: SSH Keys vs. HTTPS & PAT

Setting up passwordless, cryptographic authentication for your developer machine

Ed25519 Security
Generate Modern SSH Key
$ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"
Generating public/private ed25519 key pair...
$cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIG... user@mac
$ssh -T git@github.com
Hi username! You've successfully authenticated.
SSH (Recommended) Set once, never re-enter passwords. Used by software engineers for CLI push/pull.
HTTPS + PAT Requires Personal Access Token (classic or fine-grained) as passwords are disabled.
GitHub Settings → SSH & GPG Keys Form Verified Key

slides.title: Creating a New GitHub Repository
slides.html:
PART 03 • REPOSITORY SETUP

Creating a New GitHub Repository

Setting up the empty cloud destination for your project on GitHub.com

github.com/new

STEP-BY-STEP 5 Steps on GitHub Web

  • 1 Click the + icon at the top-right header and select New repository.
  • 2 Enter a concise Repository Name: my-app.
  • 3 Choose Public (visible to anyone) or Private (team access only).
  • 4 Click Create repository.
CRITICAL BEGINNER TRAP: If you already have code on your computer, DO NOT check "Add a README file", ".gitignore", or "license"! An empty repository allows a smooth first push without merge conflicts.

slides.title: The First Push: git push -u origin main
slides.html:
PART 04 • PUSHING CODE

The First Push: git push -u origin main

Publishing your local commit history and establishing upstream branch tracking

First Publish
Terminal: First Push Session
$git branch -M main
$git push -u origin main
Enumerating objects: 14, done.
Counting objects: 100% (14/14), done.
Writing objects: 100% (14/14), 3.24 KiB | 3.24 MiB/s, done.
* [new branch] main -> main
Branch 'main' set up to track remote branch 'main' from 'origin'.
Why the -u flag is essential: It sets the upstream reference link. Once configured, you can simply type git push or git pull without repeating "origin main" every time!
Branch Synchronized with Remote origin/main Sync Complete

PART 05 • DAILY WORKFLOW

The Daily Team Rhythm: Push & Pull

The 4-stage synchronization habit practiced by modern engineering teams

Daily Loop
1
Morning Pull: Fetch Team Updates git pull origin main Always pull before coding to prevent stale branches and merge conflicts.
2
Stage & Review Changes git add . && git status Check modified files and ensure no temporary log or build files get staged.
3
Commit with Clear Message git commit -m "feat: implement user settings" Write descriptive conventional commit messages.
4
Push to Cloud Remote git push origin <branch-name> Back up your code on GitHub and trigger automated CI test runs.
File States: Untracked → Unmodified → Modified → Staged Lifecycle

Pull Requests (PR): The Heart of GitHub Collaboration

Proposing code changes, requesting team reviews, and automated verification

Open PR

What is a Pull Request?

A Pull Request is a formal request to "pull" your feature branch commits into the main branch. It provides a dedicated collaborative space for code inspection before production release.

Base Branch Target branch to receive changes (e.g., main).
Compare Branch Source branch containing your commits (feature/auth).
PR Anatomy: A great PR includes a clear summary title, screenshots of UI changes, checklist of tested items, and tagged reviewers for sign-off.

slides.title: Merging Strategies: Merge Commit vs. Squash vs. Rebase
slides.html:
PART 06 • PULL REQUESTS

Merging Strategies: Merge Commit vs. Squash vs. Rebase

Choosing the right merge technique to maintain a pristine production history

3 Merge Types
1. Create a Merge Commit git merge --no-ff

Preserves every individual commit from the feature branch. Creates a 2-parent merge commit on main. Can make history busy if branches have many "wip" commits.

2. Squash and Merge (Industry Favorite) Recommended

Squashes 10 messy feature commits ("fixed typo", "debug logging") into 1 clean commit on main. Perfect for clean Git logs and atomic rollbacks.

3. Rebase and Merge Linear History

Appends individual commits directly onto tip of main without a merge commit. Produces a 100% linear history.

Cloning Existing Repositories: git clone

Downloading an existing remote project with full commit history

git clone
Terminal: Clone Project

Cloning into 'web-app'...
Receiving objects: 100% (452/452), 1.82 MiB | 4.12 MiB/s, done.
Resolving deltas: 100% (210/210), done.
$cd web-app && git status
On branch main. Your branch is up to date with 'origin/main'.
git init Starts a brand new, empty Git repository from scratch in an existing folder.
git clone Downloads everything, creates directory, sets up remote origin, and checks out main.

slides.title: Forks & Open Source Contribution Workflow
slides.html:
PART 07 • CLONING & CONTRIBUTING

Forks & Open Source Contribution Workflow

Contributing to public repositories you don't own with upstream sync

Fork & Upstream

5-Step Open Source Contribution Cycle

  • 1 Fork: Click "Fork" on GitHub to make a personal copy in your account.
  • 2 Clone: Clone your personal fork to your computer: git clone <fork-url>.
  • 3 Add Upstream: git remote add upstream <original-repo-url>.
  • 4 Branch & Push: git checkout -b fix-bug, commit, and push to your fork.
  • 5 Open PR: Submit a Pull Request from your fork back to the upstream repo!
Syncing your fork: Run git fetch upstream && git merge upstream/main to keep your personal fork up to date with new releases from the main team.
Upstream Organization ↔ Personal Fork ↔ Local Clone Architecture

slides.title: Resolving Merge Conflicts on GitHub & Locally
slides.html:
PART 08 • CONFLICT RESOLUTION

Resolving Merge Conflicts on GitHub & Locally

Understanding conflicting changes when team members edit the same lines of code

Conflict Fix
Conflict Markers in File app.js
<<<<<<< HEAD (Current Change - Your Branch)
const port = process.env.PORT || 3000;
======= (Divider)
const port = process.env.PORT || 8080;
>>>>>>> origin/main (Incoming Change - Teammate)
Resolution in 3 Steps: 1. Decide which version to keep (or combine both). 2. Delete all marker lines (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>). 3. Run git add . && git commit -m "fix: resolve port conflict" && git push.
Visual Conflict Editor: Accept Current vs Incoming Resolved

slides.html:
PART 09 • REPO GOVERNANCE

Protecting Production: Branch Protection Rules

Enforcing code quality, approvals, and preventing accidental main overwrites

Protected Branch

4 Essential Production Rules

🛡️
Require a pull request before mergingPrevents any developer from pushing directly to main.
👥
Require Approvals (1 or 2 peers)Guarantees at least one team engineer reviewed the code.
⚡
Require status checks to pass (CI)Unit tests, builds, and TypeScript compilation must succeed.
🚫
Block Force-Pushes & DeletionsProtects the Git history from accidental deletion or destructive resets.
Settings Location: Repo Settings → Branches → Add branch protection rule → Target: main.

slides.title: GitHub Actions: Automated Continuous Integration
slides.html:
PART 10 • AUTOMATION (CI/CD)

GitHub Actions: Automated Continuous Integration

Automatically running tests and builds on every push and pull request

CI/CD Pipeline
.github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI Tests
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
test:
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
steps:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
- run: pnpm install && pnpm test
Every pull request automatically triggers this workflow. If tests fail, GitHub blocks the merge button and notifies the team in real time!

slides.title: Top 5 GitHub Beginner Errors & Instant Fixes
slides.html:
PART 11 • BEST PRACTICES

Top 5 GitHub Beginner Errors & Instant Fixes

Practical troubleshooting solutions for the most frequent command errors

Troubleshooting
1. "error: failed to push some refs" Remote has commits you don't have. Fix: git pull --rebase origin main then push.
2. "fatal: remote origin already exists" Remote URL registered twice. Fix: git remote set-url origin <new-url>.
3. Commits not linked to your GitHub avatar Config email doesn't match GitHub. Fix: git config --global user.email "your@github.com".
4. "Support for password authentication was removed" GitHub requires SSH or PAT. Fix: Add SSH key or Personal Access Token.
5. Safely undoing a pushed bad commit Never force push on shared branches. Fix: git revert <commit-hash> && git push.
Git Undo Decision Tree: Restore vs Reset vs Revert Recovery Guide
